title: The Parable of the Rich Farmer
description: A man in the crowd asked Jesus to tell his brother to share the inheritance with him. Jesus replied that he was not appointed as a judge or arbitrator, and warned: "Beware of all greed! For a person's life does not consist in the abundance of what they possess." Then he told a parable: A rich man had land that produced well, and he did not know where to store his harvest. He decided to tear down his barns and build larger ones, gather all his grain and goods, and say to himself: "You have many good things stored up for many years. Rest easy, eat, drink and be merry!" But God said to him: "You fool! This very night your life will be demanded from you. Who then will get what you have gathered?" That is how it goes with the one who stores up treasures for themselves but is not rich toward God.

versions.title: The Parable of the Rich Fool
versions.description: A man in the crowd asked Jesus to tell his brother to share the inheritance with him. Jesus answered: "Watch out and guard yourselves against all kinds of greed!" and told a parable: There was a rich man whose land produced a good harvest. He thought: "I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, so that I can store all my grain and all my goods there. Then I will say to myself, ‘You have many years of good things stored up. Take life easy; eat, drink and be merry!’" But God said to him: "You fool! This very night your soul is required from you. Who then will get what you have prepared?" That is how it goes with the one who stores up treasures for himself but is not rich toward God.
